physical_skill: Hold a loose faucet's spout with one gripper while the other presses a lugged service key up into a hidden aerator's ribs and turns it in repeated wrist strokes (lugs out, turn back, re-engage) to break a 0.2 N m scale bond the 0.1 N m loose mount cannot react, unscrew it out of its thread (drops 4 mm onto the key), screw it back to within 15 degrees of its seat without overtightening, and take the key and fingers away.
valid_shortcuts: Red team: do nothing 0; one-arm (key only, spout not held) 0 (faucet turns past 5 degrees, latched); careless overtighten past seat 0 (latched). Turning the aerator by fingers is not possible (no part stands proud; ribs are 3 mm). Holding the key in place at the end gives at most 0.5 (key must be 3 cm away). Demo 1.0 twice (1,973 steps) on the final file.
distinct_from_nearest: No accepted or live task turns a recessed threaded part with a keyed tool while the other hand reacts its torque. 2382 is the same fixture but a different part and skill; 1540 and 1257 share the hold-while-turning pattern but turn exposed parts directly and say so in the instruction. Ours adds tool use (a lugged key engaged from below), a seized bond, out-and-back threading to a flush seat, and an unprompted counter-hold forced by physics. Residual risk: a reviewer may group it with 1540/1257 as 'hold one part while turning another', and the torques are scaled-down estimates (README states this).
